text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000006's 99215 rate is well above expected in every complexity band and is concentrated on low-complexity patients, but the few returned charts mostly support the billed level, so the picture is mixed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing side points toward upcoding: the 99215 share exceeds the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions, who account for most of the 99215s. Sampled examples include young patients billed 99215 for simple acute diagnoses such as UTI (C0005497, C0005083), upper respiratory infection (C0005382) and abdominal pain (C0004975). The documentation side points the other way, since nearly all documented 99215s support the billed level. That support is weak, though: records cover only a small share of claims, no audit trail was received, and some 'supported' notes show high MDM and long visit times for single uncomplicated diagnoses (C0005083, C0005497), with C0005083 also carrying the 'problems' note flag; this is consistent with notes possibly inflated to match the code, but does not prove it, and the no-lab mismatch is small. A reviewer should first pull full charts and audit trails for the low-complexity 99215s, starting with C0005083 and C0005497, checking whether the problem lists and documented time are clinically plausible or templated, and widen the records request beyond the current sample."}
